beats: Hook: when a model writes one word, a GPU with 132 processors (an H100 SXM's SMs) might keep only a handful busy (line_decode_idle_hall).

Recap FlashAttention (Dao et al., NeurIPS 2022; slide 36): online softmax, fuse the steps and keep the tiles on the counter (shared memory) instead of carrying bowls back to the fridge: far less memory traffic; great for training and prefill (line_decode_fused_counter; L09 plans: line_gpu_tray_fetch).

Why decode starves the GPU (slide 37): prefill splits the many queries into tiles, so S/T x heads x batch blocks; decode has one query per request, so only 1 x heads x batch blocks, far fewer than the SMs at small batch (line_decode_idle_hall).

FlashDecoding (Stanford CRFM, Oct 2023; slide 38): split the long KV cache into pieces, read them on many SMs at once, then merge the partial softmax results (the split-K idea from GEMM) (line_decode_scroll_split_readers, line_decode_merge_notes; line_scroll_reader for the long cache).

Wave quantization (slides 39, 42-45, self study): 168 blocks on 132 SMs = one full wave plus a second wave of only 36 (a bus with 132 seats and 168 passengers) (line_decode_bus_full, line_decode_bus_stragglers).
LeanAttention (2024) / stream-K (slide 39): add up all the work and deal every SM an equal share (line_decode_equal_piles).

FlashInfer (Ye et al., MLSys 2025; slide 40): the attention engine behind many serving systems: reads paged KV in place, one format for many systems, JIT-compiles custom attention variants (line_decode_mixer_attachments, line_decode_key_cutter).

POD-Attention (Kamath et al., ASPLOS 2025; slide 41): in a chunked-prefill batch, put compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode work on the same SMs so burners and pantry door are both busy (line_decode_shared_station).

Takeaway (her summary): FlashAttention for prefill, FlashDecoding for generation, FlashInfer packages them for the serving engines; scheduling, KV management and kernels are the three layers of serving.

drawings.prompt: A huge kitchen hall seen from high above and in front, a steep bird's-eye view: a regular grid of identical square cooking stations, five across and six deep (thirty in all), with clear walkways between them; at each station stands one small identical line cook (simple round face, dot eyes, a low folded paper cook's cap like a diner cook, NOT a tall chef's hat, a plain short-sleeved cook's jacket and a short apron). Only THREE stations near the front are busy: their cooks chop and stir at full speed, with small motion lines. At every other station the cook is idle: leaning on the counter, yawning, asleep with the head on folded arms, reading a small book, balancing a spoon on the nose, two of them playing cards across a walkway. Portrait image 1024x1536; the hall fills about 92% of the width and about 90% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
